title: Rochelle Ann camachile: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Rochelle Ann camachile: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Rochelle Ann camachile is a camachile variety from Andres M. Bangal. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Rochelle Ann is a registered camachile variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2014 as NSIC 2014 Cm 01. Andres M. Bangal bred it. Its record notes a yield of 80 to 100 kg.

blocks.text: Key facts about Rochelle Ann camachile
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Rochelle Ann was about 50 years old and about 12 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 80 to 100 kg. It bears regularly, with fruit in April May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of Rochelle Ann weighs about 30.44 grams, and its shape is circular. The flesh is creamy white and smooth and fine. Its sweetness measured 22.03 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 63.64 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as April May, bearing regular.
Where and when to plant Rochelle Ann camachile

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Rochelle Ann?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
